data.name: Monaco
data.region: Western Europe (French Riviera), not an EU member (customs union and VAT with France)
data.summary: Residents of Monaco pay no personal income tax (so no tax on capital gains, dividends or interest) and no wealth tax or annual property tax. Inheritance and gift tax applies only to assets situated in Monaco and is 0% between parents and children and between spouses (8% siblings up to 16% unrelated). The big exception: French nationals resident in Monaco are taxed by France as if French residents under the 1963 France-Monaco convention. Real estate purchases bear 4.5%-7.5% registration duty.

regimes.name: Ordinary Monaco residence (non-French nationals)
regimes.description: No personal income tax for residents genuinely established in Monaco. Does not apply to French nationals, who remain taxable in France on worldwide income under the 1963 Bilateral Convention (with narrow historical exceptions not researched).
regimes.eligibility: Monaco residence card (carte de séjour) and genuine establishment in Monaco. 'EU' here excludes French nationals (see description).

capital_gains.summary: No personal income tax, therefore no tax on capital gains from securities, private businesses or real estate for resident individuals.
open_questions: The government page confirms no income tax for residents but does not mention capital gains explicitly; inferred from absence of any income tax.
capital_gains.rate_basis: No personal income or capital gains tax. Foreign real estate gains may be taxed by the situs country.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Not relevant to individuals (Business Profit Tax applies only to commercial businesses with more than 25% of turnover outside Monaco).

dividends.summary: No personal income tax on dividends, domestic or foreign. Foreign withholding tax is a final cost; Monaco has very few income tax treaties, so treaty-reduced WHT is generally not available.
open_questions: Monaco's treaty network (very limited; France convention, few others) not researched in detail.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding tax on dividends (general knowledge, not verified).
dividends.treaty_network: Very limited for income tax; investors bear full non-treaty WHT on foreign dividends (e.g. 30% on US dividends without treaty).

wealth_tax.summary: No wealth tax, no annual property tax and no council tax.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: No annual property tax or council tax.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance and gift (transfer) tax applies only to property situated in Monaco, regardless of the deceased's domicile or nationality. Rate between parents and children (direct line) and spouses: 0%. Siblings 8%, uncles/aunts/nephews/nieces 10%, other relatives 13%, unrelated 16%.
open_questions: The government page applies the transfer tax to gifts of Monaco-situs property under the same situs rule but does not state separately that gift rates by relationship match the inheritance rates (0% for children is consistent with the registration-duty schedule but was not re-read).
inheritance.spouse_note: 0% between spouses and in the direct line, on property situated in Monaco (the only property taxed); the government page does not mention registered partners.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts of Monaco-situs property follow the same transfer-tax principle; 0% for children.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Only Monaco-situs assets are within scope; foreign assets are not taxed by Monaco (the deceased's nationality country may tax them, e.g. France for French nationals).
inheritance.domicile_rules: Situs-based. Declarations of inheritance must be registered within strict deadlines.

residency.tax_residency_test: No income tax, so residence matters mainly for proving non-residence elsewhere: a Monaco residence card and genuine establishment (main home, presence) are required; the tax department issues certificates of domicile/usual residence.

routes.name: Monaco residence card (carte de séjour)
routes.requirements: Accommodation in Monaco (purchase or lease), proof of sufficient means (in practice a substantial bank deposit with a Monaco bank), clean record; non-EU nationals first need a long-stay French visa. Amounts not verified.

corporate.summary: Business Profit Tax (ISB) applies only to industrial/commercial businesses earning more than 25% of turnover outside Monaco (rate not stated on the government page). VAT as in France.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Prime 4-bedroom family flat of about 200-300 m²: midpoint of the EUR 22,000-35,000 asking rents of the 4-bedroom flats in that size range listed on LuxuryEstate.com on 15 October 2026. Cross-check: prime rents average about EUR 114.50/m² a month (Jarnias, 2026: https://www.jarniascyril.com/?p=25449), i.e. about EUR 28,600 for 250 m². The same sample's median (EUR 110,000) was not used: it was dominated by 400-700 m² penthouses and duplexes in the Carré d'Or and Mareterra (EUR 70,000-190,000), far larger than the family home assumed elsewhere.

source.title: LuxuryEstate.com: luxury properties for rent in Monaco (listing sample)

intl_school_annual_fee.description: International School of Monaco, Classes 10 to 13 (upper secondary/IB) annual school fees for 2025/2026, the latest year for which the school's published terms give the fee table. One-time charges in 2025/26: application EUR 500, registration EUR 2,000, Capital Development Fund EUR 10,000 (the 2026-2027 bilingual-section terms show EUR 25,000). Sibling discounts from the third child.

source.title: The International School of Monaco: Enrolment Terms & Conditions 2025-26

cost_of_living.notes: No cost item other than rent and school fees was sourced. Real estate purchase registration duty 4.5% (transparent buyers) or 7.5%. Rent is a small listing sample; Monaco rents vary enormously with size and building, so the figure is for a 200-300 m² 4-bedroom flat, not the penthouses that dominate agency listings.

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain fully US-taxed on worldwide income; Monaco adds nothing and there is no US-Monaco income tax treaty. French nationals: taxed by France as French residents (1963 convention), so Monaco gives them no income-tax benefit.
open_questions: French nationals exception: details of the 1963 convention (e.g. historical exemption for those resident before 1957) not researched; the app should treat French citizens separately (schema only distinguishes EU/US/OTHER).
Residence card financial requirements not verified.
ISB corporate rate not stated in source opened.
School fee is the 2025/26 ISM figure; the 2026/27 tuition table was not found in the school's published 2026-2027 documents (the bilingual-section terms list a EUR 25,000 Capital Development Fund).

Indicators: the World Bank WGI (all six), life expectancy, internet use, UHC index and migrant share are present for Monaco in the pipeline data, so no WGI override is needed. Homicide rate, HDI, CPI, GDP per capita PPP and the other missing indicators have no same-definition official source located: no crime series was found on the IMSEE (Monaco Statistics) site and no police homicide count was located. They remain missing rather than proxied from France.

household_cost_detail.price_level_note: No World Bank price level for this jurisdiction; FRA's price level used for the price-scaled components.

succession.name: Monaco
succession.summary: Children are protected by a reserved share that a will cannot remove, but a person can choose their national law under the 2017 reform. Monaco has had the Hague Trusts Convention in force since 2008. Its own trust-like and foundation tools are narrow.
succession.reserved_share: Children are protected by a reserve under the Civil Code and the 2017 reform kept it. The fractions were not confirmed from a primary source.
succession.foreign_law_note: Law 1.448 of 28 June 2017: one law, that of the deceased's domicile at death, applies to the whole estate; a person may choose their national law for the whole estate (professio juris). Not under the EU Regulation.
succession.trust_note: The Hague Trusts Convention is in force since 1 September 2008 (HCCH table: accession 1 June 2007), and Law 1.448 clarifies recognition of foreign trusts. Domestic law offers a narrow fiducie (Law 214 of 1936) and foundations (Law 56 of 1922) for public-interest purposes; neither was read in detail.
open_questions: Fractions of the Monegasque reserve were not sourced.
Law 214 (fiducie) and the foundation law were identified from secondary text only; their scope was not confirmed.
Whether a choice of national law defeats the reserve for children who are Monegasque residents was not confirmed.

assumptions: The family are EU citizens who are not French nationals; French nationals resident in Monaco are taxed by France as if resident there under the 1963 France-Monaco convention (MonServicePublic, Tax in Monaco) and would need a separate recipe.

Monaco has no income tax treaty network of note, so the 15% withholding the model charges on foreign dividends is a final cost with no residence-country relief; the checks count residence-country tax only.

Only one path is modelled. Monaco taxes nothing at the personal level, so a holding company, foundation or trust cannot reduce Monaco tax; at best it adds cost. A Monegasque company that carried on a commercial business could be subject to the Business Profit Tax (ISB) (MonServicePublic, Tax in Monaco); a passive portfolio vehicle was not researched further because it brings nothing for this family.

A Monegasque patrimonial foundation is not offered: it exists only as a National Council bill (Proposition 268, reported 20 May 2026), not yet law, with a EUR 10 million cash minimum endowment (City Wealth). The older Monegasque foundations can serve only public-benefit or philanthropic aims (same source).

Inheritance is shown for an estate passing to three children. Any tax that the children's own country of residence, or a country where assets or heirs are located (for instance France on French-situs assets under the 1950 convention), may charge is outside this recipe.
open_questions: The government pages do not mention capital gains or gift duty separately; both are inferred (no income tax; same situs rule and 0% direct-line rate). Confirm with the Direction des Services Fiscaux or the Sovereign Ordinances on registration duties.

Whether a passive Monaco company or societe civile holding a securities portfolio would fall under the Business Profit Tax or be transparent was not researched; the pages opened do not address societes civiles.

Revisit the patrimonial foundation if the National Council bill (Proposition 268) is enacted: the report says the foundation would pay no income or capital gains tax if it runs no commercial business, but its assets would remain in the founder's estate for succession duty (0% in direct line) and the founder must be domiciled in Monaco.

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary residence, non-French nationals)
paths.note: Monaco levies no personal income tax on residents who are not French nationals, so dividends, interest and gains are untaxed, and there is no wealth tax or annual property tax (MonServicePublic, Tax in Monaco). Inheritance and gift duty reaches only property situated in Monaco and is 0% between parents and children and between spouses (MonServicePublic, Inheritance tax). The family is EU but not French, so the 1963 France-Monaco convention that taxes French nationals does not apply.

immigration.name: Monaco
immigration.summary: Monaco is not in the EU and everyone, EU citizens included, needs a residence card (carte de séjour) to live there more than three months. EU/EEA/Swiss citizens apply directly; US and other citizens first need a French long-stay visa. There is no fixed legal investment: the practical requirement is housing in Monaco and a bank reference, in practice a deposit of around EUR 500,000 at a Monaco bank, set by each bank.
immigration.naturalisation: Discretionary grant by the Prince; reported minimum of 10 years of residence, generally counted from age 18. Not an entitlement.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Monaco generally does not recognise dual nationality; applicants usually must renounce their previous citizenship (consultancy source, not an official text).

routes.name: Residence card on proof of means (carte de séjour)
routes.summary: A person who does not work in Monaco can get a residence card by proving housing in Monaco and sufficient resources, shown in practice by a reference from a Monaco bank. The temporary card lasts one year and is renewable.
routes.requirements: Sovereign Ordinance 3.153 of 19 March 1964, art. 7: sufficient resources if no professional activity; valid identity document; no conduct justifying refusal. Reported practice: accommodation in Monaco (title deed, a lease of 12 months or more registered with the tax department, or a sworn hosting attestation), a reference letter from a Monaco-licensed bank (market practice around EUR 500,000 on deposit, set by each bank, not by law), clean criminal record, health insurance, interview with the Sûreté Publique. EU/EEA/Swiss citizens apply directly in Monaco; US and other citizens first need a French long-stay (type D) visa. Card types reported: temporary (1 year), ordinary (3 years, after 3 years of residence), privileged (10 years, after 10 years of continuous residence).
routes.investment_options: Deposit at a Monaco bank; the amount is bank practice, not law. Private banks may ask for much more.
routes.fees_note: Official fees not sourced from a government page.
routes.physical_presence: Genuine main residence; reported 'several months a year', no published day count
routes.tax_note: Monaco levies no personal income tax on residents, except French nationals (1963 convention). A Monaco card does not by itself end tax residence elsewhere.

routes.name: Employment in Monaco (work authorisation and residence)
routes.summary: Working in Monaco needs a Monaco employer and a work authorisation; residence is then requested separately. Monaco has no digital nomad visa.
routes.requirements: Sovereign Ordinance 3.153, art. 7: a foreigner who wants to work must show authorisation from the competent authorities. Details of the employer procedure not researched.
routes.physical_presence: Place of work and housing in Monaco or neighbouring France
